discovery: Experimental realization of strongly interacting Fermi gases and the BCS-BEC crossover in ultracold atoms

nominees.name: Rudolf Grimm
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austria

nominees.name: Christophe Salomon
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, Ecole Normale Superieure, Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Using Feshbach resonances to tune interactions in degenerate atomic Fermi gases, the nominees made the BCS-BEC crossover, long a theoretical idea of Eagles, Leggett and Nozieres-Schmitt-Rink, into a controllable laboratory system. Thomas observed the first strongly interacting, hydrodynamic Fermi gas (2002). Grimm created a molecular Bose-Einstein condensate of fermion pairs and used collective modes and RF spectroscopy to reveal pairing across the crossover (2003-2004). Salomon produced molecular condensates and later measured the universal equation of state of the unitary Fermi gas with high precision (2010). Together this work established fermionic superfluidity in neutral atoms and a universal, strongly correlated quantum fluid whose physics links high-Tc superconductors, neutron stars and quark-gluon plasma. It turned cold Fermi gases into a precision tool for many-body physics and laid the groundwork for Fermi-Hubbard quantum simulation and quantum gas microscopy.
